messages:
incident-bot: [ALERT] Dedicated pool 'orpheus-dedicated' (tenant: OrpheusCorp) GPU utilization 98% for 12m, queued requests increased x3. Paging oncall. Impact: request latency > 2s for ~18% of requests. Link: https://metrics.redwood/orpheus/pool

alex: oncall here, investigating. Is this only OrpheusCorp tenant?

jamie: confirmed — single-tenant VPC pool. Queue length up, GPU busy. Autoscaler did not add nodes — hitting max_nodes=8. Current nodes: 8/8.

maya: looking at recent deploys — no rollout in last 30m. Workload spike looks generation-heavy (long seq lengths). Could kick in fallback to a quantized / lower-memory variant to reduce per-token GPU time.

oliver: customer PS note: OrpheusCorp is enterprise with 99.9% SLA. They will call if we change model. If possible, prefer capacity burst over functional fallback.

alex: options: 1) emergency burst from shared pool (+N GPUs) 2) route small percentage of traffic to redwood-small-v2 (quantized) 3) throttle non-critical background jobs for this tenant. Need decision and exec.

jamie: background jobs spike is from nightly index jobs started early — can pause. I've queued a pause: 
```
rictl jobs pause --tenant orpheus --selector indexer
```
But that only frees ~1 GPU worth.

maya: immediate cheap win: route 20% of inference requests to quantized variant via routing policy, that should cut latency for remainder while burst request spins up. Command: 
```
rictl routes update --tenant orpheus --route inference --split 80:20 --models redwood-large-v1:redwood-small-v2
```
This is safe for 2m canary, then evaluate.

oliver: customer will be unhappy but tolerable if we notify. Can we run burst in parallel?

alex: I can request burst. Because this is enterprise, we have pre-approved emergency burst + drift allowance, but requires oncall lead approval. pinging @jamie and @maya for quick ack.

jamie: ack. Approve burst request for up to 4 GPUs.

maya: ack. Also enabling prefix KV cache to drop repeat token cost. 

alex: filing burst request: 
```
rictl dedicated-burst --tenant orpheus --gpus 4 --duration 2h --reason "prod spike; queueing; customer SLA" 
```
Submitted. Waiting for cluster-controller to allocate.

incident-bot: Burst request queued (id: br-20260714-9921). Approval: auto-approve for enterprise tier pending oncall lead confirmation.

jamie: manual check — shared-pool has 6 free GPUs in region, allocation should succeed. Spawning nodes now.

(3m pass)

alex: burst applied. +4 GPUs attached. Queue dropped by ~70% within 45s. Latency back to baseline for most requests.

oliver: notifying OrpheusCorp now with incident note and mitigation steps. Keep them posted.

maya: routing change metrics look fine; model-quality checks on quantized variant look within threshold for the canary. No errors.

jamie: holding until sustained 15m of stability. If stable, we drain burst and follow up with infra changes.

alex: paging handoff in 20m to night oncall. I'll add runbook notes. Post-incident actions: bump dedicated pool min_nodes from 4->6 for OrpheusCorp, lower autoscaler target CPU/GPU threshold from 80%->70%, pre-authorize 4-GPU burst for enterprise tier, and add alert to detect long-seq generation spikes.

oliver: agreed. I'll coordinate change with customer for acceptance window.

incident-bot: Incident acknowledged by alex; status: mitigation applied (burst + routing canary). Next update in 15m or on resolution. Tags: dedicated-pool, enterprise, burst, oncall

alex: thanks team. I'll write the incident summary and owners for postmortem (owner: jamie, runbook updates: maya, customer comms: oliver).

jamie: marking as stable at +18m. Closing action: follow-up postmortem and adjust autoscaler config.

oliver: customer notified. They accepted temporary burst and asked for a weekly sync to tune autoscale.

alex: handing off to night oncall (sre-night). Full thread saved to incident tracker: https://incidents.redwood/1765439992

(End of thread)
